official.deadline_note: MEXT publishes no single central date: applicants must submit to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality by that mission's own designated deadline, which each mission sets and announces locally. MEXT states only that applicants are informed of the final selection result by their diplomatic mission after February 2027, and that grantees must in principle arrive in Japan between 1 and 7 April 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake; MEXT published the FY2027 guidelines and forms in April 2026, with arrival in Japan in April 2027 (September or October 2027 for grantees placed directly into a university's autumn term)
official.status_note: MEXT lists the FY2027 embassy-recommendation recruitment for undergraduate students under 'programmes currently being recruited' on its Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship page as of 2026-10-10.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities will be waived.
benefits: A supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month added for grantees studying or conducting research in specially designated regions
Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities will be waived

Transportation to Japan: MEXT stipulates the travel schedule and route and provides an economy-class airline ticket; a return ticket is provided on graduation for grantees returning home by the end of the final month of the scholarship period

One year of preparatory education in the Japanese language and other subjects at an institution designated by MEXT (ABK College for Social Sciences and Humanities, Osaka University for Natural Sciences)
eligibility: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; an applicant holding Japanese nationality at the time of application is not eligible, except dual nationals resident outside Japan who choose the other nationality and relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival in Japan
Age: in principle born on or after April 2, 2002

Academic background: completed 12 years of schooling outside Japan (by March 2027), or a school equivalent to a Japanese upper secondary school, or an equivalency examination, or eligibility for enrolment in a Japanese university; direct-placement applicants must satisfy one of the first, third or fourth conditions
Japanese language: willing to learn Japanese, interested in Japan, and in principle willing to carry out academic studies in Japan in Japanese
Health: able to submit a health certificate in the prescribed form signed by a physician
Arrival: in principle able to arrive in Japan between April 1, 2027 and April 7, 2027, departing the home residence on or after April 1, 2027
requirements: Applications must be submitted to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of the applicant's nationality by that mission's designated deadline
Applicants must submit two application packets: one complete set of original documents and one complete set of copies
Document numbers 1 to 9 must be written in the upper right-hand corner of the first page of each document
Documents must be written in Japanese or English, or accompanied by a translation into either language
Applicants must sit the written academic examinations and interview of the First Screening at the Japanese diplomatic mission
The First Screening must be conducted at the diplomatic mission of the country whose nationality the applicant chooses
documents: 1 Application Form (FY2027 MEXT form) with photograph
2 Direct Placement Preference Form, submitted after passing the First Screening by eligible applicants only
3 Academic transcript(s) for all school years of the school or university attended, showing the grade scale applied and the grades earned
4 Certificate(s) of graduation of the school or university attended, or a certificate of prospective graduation
5 Recommendation letter from a class teacher or principal of the last school attended
6 Medical certificate in the FY2027 MEXT certificate form
7 Certificate of enrollment (only for applicants currently enrolled in a university) and 8 certificate of university enrollment qualification examination, where applicable
9 Certificate of Japanese or English language proficiency, only if held: 2 copies, issued no earlier than two years before the date of application to the Japanese diplomatic mission
selection_criteria: The Japanese diplomatic mission conducts the First Screening through examination of submitted application documents, written academic examinations and interviews

Written examination subjects: Japanese, English and Mathematics for Social Sciences and Humanities (A and B); Japanese, English, Mathematics, Chemistry and Physics or Biology for Natural Sciences (A, B and C)
Applicants who pass the First Screening are recommended to MEXT, which conducts the Second Screening and selects candidates from each course

University placement is decided by MEXT in consultation with the university and the preparatory educational institution, taking into account First Screening results, academic achievement at the preparatory institution, the proposed major and the university's receiving capacity; no objection by the grantee is allowed
The reasons for screening results will not be disclosed
coverage: Supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month for study in specially designated regions
Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at universities
One-way economy-class airline ticket from the international airport nearest the grantee's residence to an international airport in Japan on the normal route to the accepting university
Return economy-class airline ticket from Japan to the grantee's home country on graduation
application_method: Obtain the FY2027 application guidelines and forms from the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of your nationality
Complete the Application Form and assemble the required supporting documents
Submit both the original set and the copy set to the diplomatic mission by its designated deadline
Sit the First Screening written academic examinations and interview at the diplomatic mission
Submit the Direct Placement Preference Form after passing the First Screening, if eligible
Await notification of the final selection result from the diplomatic mission after February 2027
official.application_route: Apply to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality, which runs the First Screening and recommends successful applicants to MEXT; no application fee is charged.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and must not hold Japanese nationality at the time of application; dual nationals resident outside Japan may apply if they choose the other nationality and relinquish Japanese nationality on arrival. The First Screening must be taken at the mission of the chosen country of nationality.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who apply through the Japanese diplomatic mission in their country of nationality; Japanese nationals are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must choose a Field of Study (Social Sciences and Humanities A or B, or Natural Sciences A, B or C), a Course and up to three Majors from the published table; fields of art, including music, are not majors eligible for application.
official.duration: Five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory education for grantees entering a preparatory institution; seven years, until March 2034, for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year pharmacy course; four years (six years for those fields) for grantees enrolled through direct placement.
official.description: MEXT offers scholarships to international students who wish to study at Japanese national universities as Undergraduate Students, selected on the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. Grantees receive a monthly allowance, have entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived, and are flown to Japan and home, while MEXT decides the preparatory institution and university placement. MEXT's stated aim is to foster human resources who become bridges of friendship between the grantee's country and Japan.
official.english_requirement: No English test score is required. Applicants must be willing to learn Japanese and in principle willing to carry out their academic studies in Japan in Japanese; Japanese or English language proficiency certificates may be submitted if held, and must have been issued no earlier than two years before the date of application to the Japanese diplomatic mission.

not_confirmed: deadline_central: MEXT publishes no central date; the deadline is set by each Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country of nationality
study_mode: the FY2027 guidelines do not publish a full-time or part-time designation
verification.notes: Monthly allowance of 117,000 yen, regional supplement, fee waiver, airfare, scholarship period, age and academic conditions, document list and selection process were read directly from MEXT's own FY2027 undergraduate (embassy recommendation) application guidelines PDF and the FY2027 recruitment page that publishes it.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-package award: JPY 117,000 a month (plus JPY 2,000-3,000 in specially designated regions), waivers of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at Japanese national universities, and economy-class flights to Japan and back on graduation. The route is the Japanese embassy in your own country, not a university, so the first practical step is contacting that mission early because it sets its own deadline and only nominates a limited number of candidates per country. Expect up to a year of intensive Japanese at ABK College or Osaka University before your degree begins, and plan to arrive with roughly US$2,000, since the first stipend payment only lands one to one and a half months after arrival.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent secondary-school graduates with about 12 years of schooling outside Japan, born on or after 2 April 2002, who are willing to study in Japanese and can commit to the 1-7 April 2027 arrival window.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact the Japanese embassy or consulate general covering your nationality now to confirm its own application deadline and candidate quota, because MEXT publishes no central date
Check your date of birth against the 2 April 2002 cut-off and your graduation date against the March 2027 completion requirement
Order transcripts that explicitly show the grade scale applied and grades earned for every school year, plus a certificate of (prospective) graduation
Book a physician appointment for the health certificate on the FY2027 MEXT form, and tell the mission if your health changes afterwards
Photocopy everything: submitted documents are never returned, and you must hand in two identical packets with numbers 1 to 9 written in the top right corner of each first page
Prepare for written exams in Japanese, English and Mathematics (add Chemistry and Physics or Biology for Natural Sciences); calculators are banned
Verify passport validity and budget for the new 'Student' visa, national health insurance and the first month of living costs
common_rejection_risks: Missing, mis-numbered or untranslated documents, since a file that is incomplete or inaccurate is simply not processed
Language proficiency certificates issued more than two years before the application date
Applying while already enrolled, or planning to enrol, in Japan as a privately financed student, or while applying to another MEXT programme
Having been a previous MEXT scholarship grantee, which makes you ineligible even if you withdrew after arrival
Choosing an art or music major, which is not an eligible field
Arriving outside the 1-7 April 2027 window, in which case travel expenses are not paid and you may have to withdraw
Assuming you can change university or course afterwards: transfers and course changes are not permitted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation (preparatory institution residences, university international halls and private apartments are all at your own expense), domestic travel from your home to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, special taxes, travel insurance, carry-on or unaccompanied baggage, visa costs, and the gap of roughly one to one and a half months before the first stipend payment.
document_audit: Photograph: 4.5 x 3.5 cm, upper body, full face, no hat, taken within six months, name and nationality written on the back
Transcripts must show the grade scale as well as the grades; currently enrolled students must also file a transcript when they graduate
Documents in any language other than Japanese or English need a certified translation attached
Keep personal copies of the whole packet because nothing is returned and bound documents may be dismantled during review
alerts: The monthly amount can change each fiscal year depending on the Japanese government budget
Stipend payments go only to a Japan Post Bank account opened after arrival; bring start-up cash
MEXT decides the accepting university and no objections to that decision are accepted
Grantees must enrol in National Health Insurance on arrival and are advised to obtain an Individual Number (My Number) Card
The English guidelines are a translation of the Japanese originals, which prevail in any dispute
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Collect the FY2027 pack from the Japanese diplomatic mission covering your nationality, file originals plus copies before its own deadline, sit its written exams and interview, and wait for the mission to notify the final result after February 2027.

official.deadline_note: There is no applicant-facing deadline: under the university-recommendation route the president of the accepting university files the nomination to MEXT inside a published submission window. MEXT's FY2026 notice set those windows as 5-15 January 2026 for the April 2026 term (research and undergraduate students), 20 February-5 March 2026 for the October 2026 term (research students) and 18-25 May 2026 for the October 2026 term (undergraduate students); the FY2026 general-selection research-student windows were 20 February-5 March 2026 and 9-19 March 2026 for the SATREPS and e-ASIA joint research slots. The FY2027 windows had not been published as of 2026-10-10, so an applicant's real deadline is the nominating university's internal cut-off.
official.application_cycle: Annual; MEXT issues the recruitment notice and calls universities for nominations each December for April and October arrivals in the following year (the most recently published cycle, FY2026, was issued in December 2025)
official.status_note: The FY2026 university-recommendation submission windows closed in January, March and May 2026. MEXT publishes each cycle's guidelines and windows in December, and the FY2027 university-recommendation notice had not been posted as of 2026-10-10; MEXT's 2027 intake page currently lists only the embassy-recommendation routes.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities must be paid by the accepting university.
benefits: Allowance paid according to the course enrolled in: 117,000 yen per month for regular students in bachelor degree courses, 144,000 yen per month for master's or professional degree courses, 145,000 yen per month for doctoral courses
A supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month for grantees studying or conducting research in specially designated regions
Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities must be paid by the accepting university

Transportation to Japan and back: MEXT stipulates the travel schedule and route and provides an economy-class airline ticket, including a return ticket on graduation or completion when the grantee returns home by the end of the final month of the scholarship period (no ticket is provided for domestic recommenders)
eligibility: Nomination by the accepting university: the president of each university recommends to MEXT international students deemed both exceptional and in need of scholarship, after screening at the university
Outstanding academic achievement: a Grade Point Average of 2.30 or above in the degreed or currently enrolled courses, to be maintained while receiving the scholarship
Research students must satisfy the conditions for admission to a master's or doctoral course at a Japanese graduate school, and apply in the field they majored in at university or a related field

Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, without Japanese nationality at the time of application; research students must in principle have been born on or after April 2, 1991

Language proficiency: JLPT N2 or higher, or an English proficiency test score corresponding to CEFR B2 or higher, or curricula completed mainly in Japanese or English meeting graduate admission requirements, or an equivalent judgement by the accepting university
Arrival in Japan within the period designated by MEXT or the accepting university; in principle between April 1 and April 7 for the April term
requirements: The student must be nominated by the accepting university; individual applicants cannot apply directly to MEXT under this route
Documents must reach MEXT within the published submission window; late submissions, replacements, amendments, withdrawals, re-applications and changes to nominee rankings are not permitted
Grantees must newly obtain a 'Student' residence status; arriving or studying without it cancels the scholarship
Grantees must maintain an annual GPA of at least 2.30, or the grading standard set by the university, or payment is suspended

Students in adopted five-year doctoral courses must apply for extension of the scholarship period when advancing to the third year; extension is not accepted for bachelor, preparatory education and bachelor, master's (doctoral first phase) or professional degree courses
MEXT stipulates the travel schedule and route, and the airline ticket cannot be changed after it is provided
documents: Documents filed to MEXT by the university: Recommendation Form for MEXT Scholarship Students (Appendix Form 1), Nomination List (Appendix Form 2), Report of comprehensive performance evaluation (Appendix Form 3) and Record of admission and selection in the programme (Appendix Form 4), one original each attached to the official document
Application Form with photograph (Appendix Form 5), 4.5 x 3.5 cm photo taken within the last six months, name and nationality on the back
Field of Study and Research Plan (Appendix Form 6) for research students

Documents the university requests from the student and keeps on campus: copy of passport or government-issued identification, official academic transcripts for all years of the last university or graduate school, certificate of (prospective) graduation or diploma, documents attesting to outstanding academic achievement, recommendation letter from a dean or above, thesis abstracts, and proof of language ability such as a TOEFL, IELTS or JLPT score report or a language-of-education certificate
selection_criteria: University screening first: the nominating university screens applicants in its own admission and selection process and ranks nominees for each priority placement of its adopted programme
MEXT's selection committee decides the candidates among those recommended, and MEXT decides the scholarship grantees and the periods of scholarship

Academic achievement is judged against a GPA of 2.30 or above; where a GPA cannot be calculated from the transcript, a recommendation letter from a dean or above clearly stating that the applicant's ranking is within the top 30% is deemed equivalent

Where language ability is established by the accepting university's own judgement rather than a test, the university must state its reasons in the Report of comprehensive performance evaluation and attach supporting documents
Grantees are notified to the president of each university by official announcement; MEXT does not notify the grantee directly
coverage: Monthly allowance of 144,000 yen for regular students in master's or professional degree courses and 145,000 yen for doctoral students (117,000 yen for bachelor degree courses)
Supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month in specially designated regions
Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees paid by the accepting university
Economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on graduation or completion of the course, back to the grantee's home country
application_method: Identify a Japanese university that holds MEXT university-recommendation slots, including adopted programmes under the special selection or the general selection with SATREPS and e-ASIA joint research slots
Apply to that university in its own intake for international research students and secure its acceptance
The university screens candidates, ranks the nominees and files the nomination package to MEXT within the published submission window
MEXT's selection committee reviews the nominations and MEXT confirms the grantees and scholarship periods
The university president is notified of the result and directs the grantee to contact the Japanese diplomatic mission for visa procedures
official.application_route: You cannot apply to MEXT yourself: win a place at a Japanese university that nominates you under the university-recommendation route, and that university's president files the recommendation to MEXT inside the published window.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and must not hold Japanese nationality at the time of application; dual nationals resident outside Japan may apply if they choose the other nationality and renounce Japanese nationality on arrival. Applicants already in Japan may be nominated as domestic recommenders, but they must not exceed 40% of total candidates.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students worldwide, including those already residing in Japan as medium- to long-term residents or as privately financed students, subject to the 40% cap on domestic recommenders.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research students should apply for the field of study they majored in at university or a related field, and it must be a subject they will be able to study and research at the accepting university. Selection runs through MEXT's adopted-programme special selection and the general selection (general, SATREPS and e-ASIA joint research slots).
official.research_requirement: Research students must submit a Field of Study and Research Plan (Appendix Form 6) and, where required, thesis abstracts of previous work; the proposed research must match a field the accepting university can supervise.
official.duration: The necessary period for the completion of the respective regular course. If the university term begins in the middle of the month, no scholarship is paid for that month. For adopted five-year doctoral courses, years one and two count as a master's course and years three to five as a doctoral course, so an extension application is required when advancing to the third year.
official.description: MEXT's aim is to foster human resources who will become bridges of friendship between the grantee's country and Japan through study in Japan and who will contribute to the development of both countries and the wider world. Under the university-recommendation route the accepting university nominates research students, the university pays the education fees, and MEXT pays the monthly allowance and the airfare for the necessary period of the regular course.
official.english_requirement: Applicants must satisfy one of the published conditions: pass JLPT at N2 or higher at the time of application; complete curriculums that meet the conditions for admission to a master's or doctoral course at a Japanese graduate school using Japanese as the main language; or be regarded by the accepting university as having Japanese ability equivalent or better. Alternatively in English: achieve a score in an English language proficiency test corresponding to CEFR B2 or higher at the time of application; complete such curriculums using English as the main language; or be regarded by the accepting university as having English ability equivalent or better.

not_confirmed: deadline_central: FY2027 university-recommendation submission windows had not been published as of 2026-10-10, and no applicant-facing deadline exists under this route
study_mode: the guidelines do not publish a full-time or part-time designation
verification.notes: Allowance rates, fee payment by the accepting university, airfare, GPA 2.30 rule, language conditions, nomination documents and submission windows were read directly from MEXT's university-recommendation application guidelines PDF and its FY2026 recruitment notices; the master's and doctoral rates were cross-checked against MEXT's FY2027 research-student guidelines, which publish the same figures, and the language conditions against MEXT's language-requirements notice for university recommenders.

applicant_utility.summary: Under this route the university, not the applicant, files the nomination, so the work is winning a place at a Japanese university that holds a MEXT university-recommendation slot rather than filling in a scholarship form. Grantees receive JPY 144,000 a month in a master's or professional degree course and JPY 145,000 in a doctoral course, the accepting university pays the entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and MEXT buys the flights home and back. Two gates decide your chances early: a GPA of at least 2.30 maintained throughout, and language evidence at JLPT N2 or CEFR B2 level. Because the university must file inside MEXT's fixed window, your real deadline is the university's internal cut-off, which normally falls weeks or months before MEXT's.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong Master's or doctoral candidates with a GPA of 2.30 or above and N2-level Japanese or B2-level English who can persuade a Japanese university to accept and then nominate them.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist Japanese universities that run MEXT university-recommendation nominations, including adopted programmes under the special selection and the general selection, SATREPS and e-ASIA joint research slots
Contact prospective supervisors before applying, since the nomination depends on a real acceptance and a research field the university can supervise
Document your GPA precisely; if your institution does not calculate a GPA, obtain a dean's letter stating that you rank in the top 30% of your faculty
Book JLPT N2 or a CEFR-B2-equivalent English test in good time, or obtain a certificate showing your degree was taught mainly in Japanese or English
Ask the university which appendix forms it needs from you and its internal filing date, then work backwards from MEXT's January to March window
Keep passport, transcripts, graduation certificate, thesis abstracts and a dean's recommendation letter ready in Japanese or English, with translations if needed
Confirm you can newly obtain a 'Student' residence status and arrive within the accepting university's designated arrival period
common_rejection_risks: Letting your annual GPA fall below 2.30 or the university's own standard, which suspends payment and can cancel the award
Withdrawing, transferring to another university, or moving to the doctoral phase without an approved extension of the scholarship period
Entering or continuing study without a 'Student' status of residence, including domestic recommenders who never switch status
The university filing an incomplete or inaccurate nomination list or application form, which MEXT warns is the most common error and is not processed at all
Missing MEXT's submission window, or asking to amend, replace or withdraw documents afterwards, none of which is permitted
Holding or planning another scholarship funded by the Japanese government or a government-related organisation
Losing degree intent, since applicants with no intention to obtain a degree are ineligible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic recommenders receive no airfare at all, so travel both ways is self-funded. Grantees still pay domestic travel to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel within Japan, travel insurance and baggage, plus accommodation where the accepting university does not provide it, and the first one to one and a half months of living costs before the first payment.
document_audit: Nomination List and Application Form are the forms MEXT says are most often filled in incorrectly, so have a second person at the university check every field before filing
Everything must be in Japanese or English, or carry a translation, and should be A4 word-processed where possible
Submitted documents are not returned, so keep certified personal copies of transcripts and graduation certificates
The university must hold one on-campus copy of every document it requests from you and be able to produce it on MEXT's request
alerts: Domestic recommenders cannot exceed 40% of total nominees and never receive travel expenses
If the university term starts mid-month, no scholarship is paid for that month
In adopted five-year doctoral courses you must apply for extension when moving into year three, or payments stop
If you later re-apply through the general selection instead of extending, you count as a previous MEXT grantee and are ineligible unless one of the narrow exceptions applies
Results are announced to the university president, so chase the university, not MEXT, and expect the university to require an official pledge to MEXT's rules before the award is confirmed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure admission at a participating Japanese university, which screens and ranks you and files the nomination package to MEXT inside the published window; MEXT's selection committee confirms the award and notifies the university president, who passes the result to you.
